#  41506 - Modelling Business Processes, Workflow and Information Management Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **41506 - module is no longer offered from WS 2011/12**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Modelling Business Processes, Workflow and Information Management**  |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 4 - Environmental Sciences and Process Engineering   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. PD Dr.-Ing. habil. Molkenthin, Frank 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every winter semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | Capacities for analysis, modelling and implementation of business processes; Capacities about theory of sets and graphs; Ability to model using Unified Modelling Language; Implementation using OO-Java; Concepts for design, options and experiences from the profession; Application to real world problems.  |  
| Contents:  | Mapping the potential of ICT to support business processes (workflow) will be taught. Basic mathematics of theory of sets and graphs will be presented and ICT oriented model description formulation introduced (UML, unified modelling language). Examples will be modelled taken from hydroinformatics system appliation. Information systems for coastal zone management. Meta data and information classification for hydroinformatics systems.  |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Lecture / 40 Hours 
  * Exercise / 40 Hours 
  * Practical training / 40 Hours 
  * Self organised studies / 60 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | see http://euroaquae.tu-cottbus.de  |  
| Module Examination:  | Unspecified - Specification from winter semester 2016/17 required!  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | exercises, written and oral examination  |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | Lecturers: Molkenthin, external: Lehfeldt and Huhnt  |
